seoTitle: How to Combine Two Indicators in TradingView with ChatGPT
metaDescription: Learn how to merge two Pine Script indicators — like RSI and MACD — into one TradingView script using ChatGPT, with alerts and testing included.
intro: Running RSI and MACD as two separate indicators means two panels competing for chart space and no easy way to combine their signals. Merging them into one Pine Script fixes both problems, but writing that merge by hand means dealing with duplicate input names, mismatched version headers, and plot conflicts. This guide walks through using ChatGPT to generate each indicator individually, verify it works alone, then merge both into a single combined script — following the actual code and chart output from a real RSI-and-MACD merge, right down to the finished indicator running on a live BTCUSD chart.

steps.heading: Generate each indicator separately first
steps.body: Before asking for a merge, get ChatGPT to write out each indicator as its own clean, working script — one labeled "RSI Indicator Only," the other "MACD Indicator Only." Each one starts with the version header and indicator() declaration, followed by clearly separated Inputs, Calculation, Plots, and Alerts sections. Keeping them separate at this stage matters because it's much easier to spot a mistake in a 20-line single-indicator script than in a 60-line combined one, and you'll reuse these exact input names when you ask for the merge in the next step.

image.caption: ChatGPT's standalone RSI script — inputs for period, overbought, and oversold levels, then the plot and alertcondition lines, before anything gets merged.

steps.heading: Test each script alone on your chart
steps.body: Paste the first script into TradingView's Pine Editor and click Update on chart to confirm it actually compiles and plots correctly before you complicate anything. In the example run, the MACD-only script adds its line, signal line, and histogram in a separate panel below a live BTCUSD five-minute chart, with the indicator name and settings shown right in the panel header. If a single indicator throws an error at this stage, fix it here — debugging one script is far simpler than debugging two scripts that have already been mashed together.

image.caption: The MACD script running alone in a lower panel under the BTCUSD chart, confirmed working before it gets combined with RSI.

steps.heading: Ask ChatGPT to merge the two into one script
steps.body: With both scripts verified individually, paste them into the same ChatGPT conversation and ask it to combine them into a single indicator. Tell it explicitly to rename any clashing variables — both scripts likely used similar names for length or smoothing inputs — and to keep the indicator title descriptive, something like "RSI & MACD Combo." A good merge keeps the same Inputs / Calculation / Plots / Alerts structure as the originals, just with both indicators' logic living under one indicator() declaration instead of two.

steps.heading: Decide overlay or separate panel before you paste
steps.body: RSI and MACD are both oscillators that don't belong on the price chart itself, so tell ChatGPT to set overlay=false and keep the combined output in its own panel below price — that's the correct default for this particular pairing. If you were instead combining something like a moving average with price action, you'd want overlay=true so it draws directly on the candles. Specifying this up front avoids a second round-trip to fix the display after you've already pasted and tested the code.

steps.heading: Paste the merged script and add it to the chart
steps.body: Copy the final combined code from ChatGPT, paste it into a fresh Pine Editor tab, and click Update on chart. In the finished example, the combined "RSI & MACD Combo" indicator renders both the RSI line and the MACD line, signal, and histogram together in a single lower panel under the same BTCUSD chart — one script, one panel, both signals visible at once instead of stacked across two separate indicators.

image.caption: The merged RSI & MACD Combo indicator running in one panel below the chart — both oscillators plotted from a single Pine Script after the merge.

steps.heading: Fix compile errors by pasting them back into ChatGPT
steps.body: If the merged script throws an error on paste, don't try to hand-debug unfamiliar Pine Script syntax — copy the exact error message TradingView shows and paste it straight back into the ChatGPT conversation along with the script. Most merge errors come from duplicate variable names ChatGPT missed, a version mismatch between the two original scripts, or a plot() call left over from one script that conflicts with the other. Naming the specific error gets a working fix far faster than describing the symptom in your own words.

steps.heading: Add combined alert conditions
steps.body: Both original scripts already had their own alertcondition() calls — RSI crossing overbought or oversold, MACD crossing its signal line. Once merged, ask ChatGPT to add a new alertcondition that fires only when both are true at once, using an if-then check like a MACD bullish crossover happening while RSI is below its oversold line. That combined condition is usually the whole reason to merge two indicators in the first place — a single alert that only fires when both signals agree, instead of two separate alerts you have to cross-reference yourself.

faq.question: Do I need coding experience to combine indicators using ChatGPT?
faq.answer: Not necessarily — ChatGPT can generate and merge the Pine Script code for you, though testing each indicator alone first, as covered above, helps you spot problems before they get buried in a combined script.

faq.question: Can ChatGPT make mistakes when merging Pine Script code?
faq.answer: Yes — duplicate variable names and version mismatches are the most common issues. Paste the exact TradingView error message back into ChatGPT rather than describing it, and it can usually fix it in one pass.

faq.question: Should combined oscillators like RSI and MACD use overlay=true or false?
faq.answer: False — both are oscillators that plot in their own panel below the price chart, not on top of the candles, so overlay=false is the correct setting for this kind of pairing.

faq.question: Can I combine more than two indicators into one script?
faq.answer: Yes, the same generate-test-merge approach extends to three or more, though it's worth testing each one alone first even more carefully as the combined script grows.

faq.question: Will combining indicators automatically create a combined alert?
faq.answer: No — each original script keeps its own separate alertcondition() calls after merging. You need to explicitly ask ChatGPT to add a new alert that checks both indicators' conditions together.
